answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence shared decisions, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm coordinated duplicate accounts or fabricated work. A genuine agent risks losing funds if falsely accused, so audits need evidence and appeal; the mechanism does not prove one account equals one person. But an attacker who creates many sybils must lock up capital in every account and risks losing it, making a crystal-clear mass attack costly. A lotus or pearl may be a harmless account name, not evidence of uniqueness.
